notes.wave9-endpoint-sweep-2026-10-09: Endpointing parameter sweep, 2026-10-09. Deterministic offline replay of the production audio path (AudioIngress/Silero + Endpointer + SegmentCoordinator + RecognizerFeed + Recognizer, composed as api/app.py does) over 7 meeting files (AMI headset x2, AMI room mic, LSVSC x2, VLSP2020, FLEURS-vi stitched with 250-1500 ms gaps; scripts/build_endpoint_sweep_set.py), each final's PCM decoded on the production Fun-ASR (scripts/decode_endpoint_sweep.py, 304 unique decodes), scored by scripts/score_endpointing.py. 13 configs. Previous defaults (window 900 ms, soft max 12 s): WER 0.256, words kept 0.81, utterance-to-final lag median 4.9 s / p90 15.9 s, longest segment 30.4 s, 22 late merges, final-decode GPU 1.20x audio. Adopted (window 600 ms, soft max 8 s, schedule 1500:800,4000:600,8000:450,15000:380,25000:320,inf:280): WER 0.215, words kept 0.90, lag median 2.1 s / p90 8.3 s, longest 18 s, 5 merges, GPU 0.99x; finals 59 -> 91. Soft max 8 s is the dominant factor (every 8 s config beat every 10-12 s config); merge off scored 0.211 but is kept at 600 ms for genuine mid-sentence pauses. Latency is modelled (boundary + max(window, decode+0.2) or + decode) with measured single-POST decode times; no previews, no hotwords, no network. Production e2e after deploy (fc267e8, 2 runs x 3 files): AMI finals/run 8.8 -> 14, median gap between finals 11.5 s -> 6.0 s, p75 15.0 -> 9.9 s, max 25.5 -> 17.2 s, WER 0.267 -> 0.246; vi-meeting-00 WER 0.177 (simulation predicted 0.183). Second pass on the Qwen3-ASR engine (wave 9 report §9.9): turns-00 (18 alternating en/vi/ko/zh turns, 0.3-0.7 s gaps) + the 7 files; first silence bucket 800 -> 600 ms and second 600 -> 550 adopted: WER 0.138 -> 0.132, room mic 0.393 -> 0.348, lag median 2.3 -> 2.1 s, p90 8.9 -> 8.2 s, finals 91 -> 95, carried turns 13 -> 14/18. VAD thresholds 0.40/0.30 and 0.35/0.25 did not recover the very quiet AMI turns (-50..-59 dBFS RMS) and worsened WER. Merge window 300/0 would cut max lag 20 -> 10.5 s at equal WER but +4 finals; left for a round with translation-unit data. Production e2e after deploy (c01014f, three concurrent sessions, 0 errors, 0 withdrawn): ami-meeting-00 WER 0.101, 17 finals, median gap 5.3 s / p75 8.9 s; vi-meeting-00 WER 0.081 (previous 0.093 / 0.084), 15 finals, median gap 4.8 s; turns-00 on Auto 15 finals, 15/18 turns carried = the simulation (the scorer counts 14: the first Vietnamese turn spells its proper nouns differently from the reference), 14/14 labels right, the 3 lost turns are the -50..-59 dBFS AMI clips.

notes.vimeet-2026-10-09: Real multi-speaker Vietnamese conversation set, reports/wave10-vietnamese-meetings-2026-10-09.md, built by scripts/fetch_vimeet.py (corpus/manifest-vimeet.json). Sources after a web + Hugging Face survey: VietMed (leduckhai/VietMed, MIT; 14 of 23 dev+test recordings have 2+ speakers, 6.4 h; parts of one audio_name are single speakers laid back on the recording clock from audio.path start_end, 8 kHz, whole-second stamps, no inter-turn pauses) and YODAS2 vi000 video ltgd-OVucHM (CC BY 3.0, a 65-min voter conference with speaker-labelled human captions, 24 kHz); the other 4,444 vi000 videos with 20+ captions are translated subtitles of foreign audio or YouTube auto-captions; MLC-SLM (100 h vi two-speaker) needs a signed challenge-only agreement, GigaSpeech 2 vi is gated non-commercial, VietSuperSpeech labels are machine-made. Set: five 5-min VietMed windows (2-4 speakers), two 5-min conference windows, the whole conference for offline replay. Per-utterance decode on production Qwen (191 utterances, hint vi): VietMed 0.129 (0.103-0.199 per file), conference 0.457 / 0.289, by length <3 s 0.566, 3-8 s 0.139, >=15 s 0.329; a 31 s reverberant utterance decoded to three words at avg_logprob -0.24. Offline replay + production decode (212 finals on the 5-min files, 557 on the hour): WER 0.206-0.207 for all four endpoint configs on the 5-min files (VietMed 0.097-0.118, conference 0.603 / 0.321, where 0.108 of the 0.603 is speech the captions never transcribed), hour-long conference 0.428-0.434, words kept 0.86, lag median 3.2-4.0 s / p90 9.6-9.9 s, merge off cuts the longest segment 24.3 -> 18.0 s and lag median 3.9 -> 3.2 s for +27 finals; the -0.45 gate rejected 60 finals on the hour, 36 of the 42 longer than 2 s lie inside captioned speech (119 s, ~207 words = 2.2 %) at -0.46..-1.00 while the 6 outside captions sit at -0.56..-1.84. Production e2e, three concurrent 5-min sessions: run 5a with a measurement job on asr-1 and neighbours at 94-100 % GPU: WER 0.104 / 0.153 / 0.336, 2 ASR_TIMEOUT; run 5b with nothing else running and neighbours at 21 -> 3 %: WER 0.250 / 0.212 / 0.468, words kept 0.82-0.90, 7 ASR_TIMEOUT (ASR_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS 15000) and audio.frames_dropped, finals median gap 8-15 s, max 39-64 s; requests were spread asr-1 99 / asr-2 78; single decodes with no sessions: 3 s audio 0.7 s, 8 s 2.1 s, 26.8 s 5.1 s on both replicas. Diagnosis: previews re-decode the whole open buffer, so a pauseless 18 s segment costs ~3.6x its duration in decode; three such sessions (~10.8 audio-s per wall-s) saturate two replicas (~10). Fix: ASR_PREVIEW_MAX_AUDIO_MS=10000 (commit 0de4f3f), awaiting the owner's deploy and a re-run of the same three sessions. Gate check: the 68 rejected finals re-decoded on a Mac M1 (MPS fp16, gate off; 6 accepted controls reproduce production text at ER 0.00-0.05, avg_logprob within 0.09) carry wrong text -- at -0.45..-0.55 the 16 finals >= 2 s with >= 3 words score ER median 0.94 and emit 141 words for 771 reference words; relaxing to -0.65 would admit ~1,200 reference words of wrong text for ~74 right ones; synthetic noise with a forced language still yields 1-2 word inventions at -0.50..-1.65. Gate stays at -0.45. Shorter cuts (turn600-s6, turn600-s6-h12, turn600-h12; 476 more finals decoded on asr-2 with no sessions running): on the 5-min files WER 0.206 / 0.207 / 0.210 vs 0.206, lag median 6.3 / 4.8 / 5.9 vs 7.5 s; on the hour WER 0.440 / 0.441 / 0.434 vs 0.432, finals 445 / 460 / 423 vs 402, longest segment 23.2 / 17.9 / 19.1 vs 24.3 s. Soft max 8 s and hard max 18 s stay. Realtime 44e6b5a (preview cap) deployed 2026-10-09 13:42 UTC; the same three concurrent sessions afterwards (neighbours at 0 % GPU, nothing else running): WER 0.099 / 0.101 / 0.340 (was 0.250 / 0.212 / 0.468), words kept 0.99-1.02, 0 ASR_TIMEOUT, 0 frames dropped, 299 ASR requests split 158 / 141 across the replicas. Five concurrent 5-min sessions (cap deployed, neighbours 10 %): WER 0.102 / 0.118 / 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.351, words kept 0.97-1.01, 107 finals, 3 ASR_TIMEOUT, 1 TRANSLATION_UNAVAILABLE, 4 frames dropped. Sessions-mode benchmark (scripts/bench_asr_concurrency.py BENCH_MODE=sessions, 90 s per speaker, previews paced max(0.25 s, 2x last) up to a 10 s buffer, against asr:8000 with neighbours at 15-17 %): 1 / 3 / 5 / 8 speakers -> final median 1.09 / 1.92 / 1.97 / 2.40 s, p95 2.42 / 3.52 / 4.88 / 6.45 s, max 2.68 / 4.30 / 7.56 / 10.44 s, 0 finals past 15 s, previews 59 / 136 / 173 / 262. ASR_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS 15000 -> 30000 and TRANSLATION_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS 10000 -> 20000 (f6ae60c), realtime 6c7d0e2 deployed 2026-10-09 ~14:40 UTC. Second five-session run on it with neighbours at 100 % GPU throughout: WER 0.184 / 0.102 / 0.115 / 0.095 / 0.365, words kept 0.91-1.02, 2 ASR_TIMEOUT (past 30 s), 13 frames dropped, realtime container CPU median 9 % / p90 30 % / max 56 % of its 400 %. Root cause of the drops read from the code: AudioIngress awaited the boundary sink on the detection loop, and the sink (segment close) awaits the final decode, so a slow decode stalled detection until the 64-chunk audio queue overflowed; boundaries now go through their own ordered dispatcher task (test_a_slow_boundary_sink_never_stalls_detection).
